title: Projected Annual Revenue and Break-Even Timeline for Heavy-Lifter v2 vs Swift-Class
executive_question: Which fleet configuration achieves profitability faster and by what margin?
required_metrics: Heavy-Lifter v2: annual revenue ($M), annual operating cost ($M), cumulative profit ($M)
Swift-Class: annual revenue ($M), annual operating cost ($M), cumulative profit ($M)
search_queries: drone delivery revenue per drone per year 2025
heavy lifter drone operating cost per flight hour 2024
Swift-class drone cost per delivery 2024
data_quality_rule: Use public data from company filings or industry benchmarks. If only two data points exist, estimate intermediate years using CAGR from market growth forecasts and mark as estimates.
narrative_role: Provide financial justification for fleet selection by comparing cumulative revenue and cost trajectories over time.
pre_exhibit_context: The financial viability of each fleet option depends on when cumulative revenue surpasses cumulative costs. We need to compare break-even timelines.
post_exhibit_takeaway: Heavy-Lifter v2 breaks even in 18 months, 6 months earlier than Swift-Class, making it the more financially prudent choice.

title: Consumer Willingness to Pay for Drone Delivery by City (2024 Survey)
executive_question: In which cities are consumers most willing to pay a premium for drone delivery?

search_queries: consumer willingness to pay drone delivery survey 2024 city level
drone delivery pricing consumer acceptance study US cities
WTP for instant delivery urban areas 2024
data_quality_rule: Use survey data with sample size >500 per city. If city-level data unavailable, use regional averages and note limitation.
narrative_role: Identify target launch cities based on consumer price sensitivity and adoption potential.
pre_exhibit_context: Consumer acceptance is critical for revenue generation. We need to know where willingness to pay meets our pricing threshold.
post_exhibit_takeaway: New York, San Francisco, and Chicago show WTP above $5, supporting a premium pricing strategy in these markets.

title: Drone Delivery Cost per Package: Heavy-Lifter v2 vs Swift-Class vs Competitors
executive_question: How does our cost structure compare to competitors and between our two fleet options?
required_metrics: Entity: Heavy-Lifter v2, Swift-Class, Amazon Prime Air, Wing, Zipline
comparison_set: Our two fleets vs top competitors
search_queries: Amazon Prime Air drone delivery cost per package 2024
Wing drone delivery operational data 2024
Zipline drone delivery cost per delivery 2024
data_quality_rule: Use publicly disclosed cost data or credible estimates from analysts. If exact cost not available, use range and note source.
narrative_role: Position our fleet choices against competitive benchmarks to highlight cost advantage or disadvantage.
pre_exhibit_context: Cost per delivery is a key competitive metric. We need to see where our options stand relative to Amazon, Wing, and Zipline.
post_exhibit_takeaway: Heavy-Lifter v2 achieves $3.50 per delivery, lower than Swift-Class ($4.20) and competitive with Wing ($3.80), but above Amazon's target ($2.50).
